notes:
Continuity

  • $f$ is continuous at $x=a$ if $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)=f(a)$.
  • Sum, difference, product, quotient (denominator $\ne0$) and composition of continuous functions are continuous.
  • Polynomial, $\sin x$, $\cos x$, $e^x$ are continuous everywhere; $\tan x$ is discontinuous where $\cos x=0$; $|x|$ is continuous everywhere but not differentiable at $0$.

Differentiability

  • $f$ is differentiable at $a$ if $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}$ exists (left derivative = right derivative).
  • Differentiability $\Rightarrow$ continuity, but not conversely (e.g. $|x|$ at $0$).

  • Product rule: $(uv)'=u'v+uv'$. Quotient rule: $\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)'=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$.
  • Chain rule: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy}{dt}\cdot\dfrac{dt}{dx}$.
  • Implicit differentiation: differentiate both sides w.r.t. $x$, treating $y$ as a function of $x$ (use chain rule for $y$ terms).
  • Logarithmic differentiation: for $y=f(x)^{g(x)}$, take $\ln$ both sides then differentiate: $\dfrac{y'}{y}=g'(x)\ln f(x)+g(x)\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}$.
  • Parametric: if $x=f(t),\,y=g(t)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$.

Higher order derivatives & key theorems

  • $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is the derivative of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ w.r.t. $x$.
  • Rolle's theorem: if $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable on $(a,b)$ and $f(a)=f(b)$, then $\exists\,c\in(a,b)$ with $f'(c)=0$.
  • Mean Value Theorem: under the same continuity/differentiability conditions, $\exists\,c\in(a,b)$ with $f'(c)=\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$.

Exam tip

KCET usually asks 3-4 questions from this chapter — checking continuity/differentiability at a point, standard derivative rules (chain, product, implicit, parametric, logarithmic), and occasionally Rolle's/MVT value of $c$. Master differentiating $\sin^{-1},\cos^{-1},\tan^{-1}$ composite forms — they appear often.
